newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Interest for Stadshypotek falls - paper.
newsitem.headline: Interest for Stadshypotek falls - paper.

text.p: Interest for the state's 34 percent stake in Swedish mortgage bank Stadshypotek has fallen off and several parties, including S-E-Banken, will not be in the auction, a Swedish newspaper reported on Monday.
The Swedish government has announced that it will hold a controlled auction to sell the state's holding in the bank.
Bids for the auction were due by 0900 GMT on Monday.
Business daily Dagens Industri quoted sources as saying two foreign parties were interested in the stake, including Finnish commercial banking group Merita Oy and GE Capital.
But Merita on Monday said it would not make a bid for Stadshypotek.
Dagens Industri said Swedish state-owned Nordbanken and commercial bank Handelsbanken were considering bids.
Finance Minister Erik Asbrink last week said the ministry had received several enquiries from parties interested in the shareholding, which the government wanted to sell to an industrial investor.
Last week, after the government announced the sale of the state's 34 percent holding, Stadshypotek and insurer Skandia announced a proposed merger.
Asbrink has criticised the board of Stadshypotek for announcing a merger without consulting him first.
